hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate (0.0774 to 1) causes divergence or unstable training, whereas the same step elsewhere helps.
At very small learning rates the network is undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing it gives large gains.
With a tiny learning rate, a larger batch means fewer updates and so more undertraining.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise, which stabilizes training at large learning rates.
Large batches give few update steps, so a higher learning rate compensates.
Small batches already give many noisy updates, so a higher learning rate tends to destabilize training.
Wider networks learn faster per step, which offsets the undertraining caused by a small learning rate.
Wide layers with large learning rates produce large effective updates and instability.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to divergence at high learning rates.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty (0.129 to 1) underfits, while the same step at small alpha is nearly neutral.
